court: In the High Court of Madras
appellants: C.H. Robinson Worldwide Freight India Private Limited Rep. by Seshachalam Center … Appellant(s);
respondents: Assessment Unit, National Faceless Assessment Centre, Through: Commissioner of Income-tax and Another … Respondent(s).
case_number: WP No. 11948 of 2024 and WMP No. 11967 of 2026
advocates: For Respondent(s): Mr. Avinash Krishnan Ravi, Jr. SC
prayer: PRAYER: Writ petition is filed under Article 226 of the Constitution of India, pleased to issue a writ of certiorarified Mandamus, to call for the records of the 1st Respondent pertaining to order dated 27-3-2024 having DIN ITBA/AST/S/143(3)/2023-24/1063477449(1) and quash the same, and consequently direct the 1st Respondent to grant a personal hearing to the petitioner and consider the submissions afresh and thus render justice.
judgment_text:
The Order of the Court was delivered by

Senthilkumar Ramamoorthy, J.:— An assessment order dated 27-3-2024 was challenged primarily on the ground of breach of principles of natural justice. After noticing that the petitioner had requested for a hearing by video conference by communication dated 25-3-2024 and that the impugned assessment order was issued on 27-3-2024 without providing such hearing, I granted an interim stay of further proceedings after recording as under:

“3. Clause (VIII) of sub-section (6) of Section 144B of the Income Tax Act makes a hearing through video conference mandatory if requested for by the assessee. On perusal of the petitioner's reply dated 25-3-2024, it is clear that the petitioner requested for a hearing through video conference. Since such video conference hearing was not provided, a prima facie case is made out. Therefore, there will be an interim stay of further proceedings pursuant to the order impugned herein until the matter is heard next.”

2. The revenue mentioned the matter for listing today. The learned Standing Counsel for the income tax Department submits that it is intended to initiate revision proceedings under Section 263 of the I-T Act and that a clarification is required as to whether the interim order would stand in the way of such proceedings.

3. The learned counsel for the assessee submits that proceedings under Section 263 are being initiated primarily to make a reference to the Transfer Pricing Officer and that this would have an impact on assessment proceedings.

4. As is evident from the above paragraphs, the ground on which I had interfered was the failure to provide a hearing by video conference, as mandated by clause (viii) of sub-section (6) of Section 144-B of the statute. The learned counsel for the revenue is unable to provide proof that such video conference hearing was given. In these circumstances, the impugned assessment order is set aside and the matter is remanded to the assessing officer for fresh hearing in accordance with law. The writ petition is disposed of on these terms. No costs. Consequently, the connected writ miscellaneous petition is closed.
